title.narrative: Food assistance to vulnerable families in Takhar Province through cash for food

description.narrative: Cordaid proposes to target the most vulnerable shock-affected households (HHs) in Takhar province, including those impacted by natural drought and people in IPC 3 & 4 due to drought and food insecurity.

Takhar Province faces significant food security challenges, exacerbated by ongoing drought and economic instability. The IPC analysis for 2024 highlights a critical situation and confirmed by cordaid raped need assesment, with many households in IPC Phase 3 (Crisis) and Phase 4 (Emergency) due to climatic shocks like irregular rainfall and drought, severely impacting agriculture. Economic challenges, including high food prices and limited livelihood opportunities, further exacerbate the situation. Humanitarian assistance remains crucial to support the affected populations and prevent further deterioration. FAO 2024 DIEM data indicate severe food consumption gaps and a high prevalence of acute malnutrition, with reduced crop yields and livestock losses. Furthermore, the ICCT 2024 prioritization underscores significant humanitarian needs, particularly during the winter months, identifying Takhar as a high-priority area due to overlapping vulnerabilities across multiple sectors, including limited access to essential services. In response, targeted interventions, such as cash-for-food program, are crucial to ensure sustained access to food for the most vulnerable HHs, including those led by women and individuals with disabilities. These efforts aim to stabilize food security and support recovery in Takhar Province and for a comprehensive response, before cash-for-food distributions, Cordaid will conduct thorough needs and market assessments to feed into the CVWG-supported JMMI

The objective of the project is to provide emergency assistance to the most vulnerable households affected by Natural disasters to improve their food security in the districts of Yangi Qala, Namak ab, and chal of Takhar province. It will be unconditional cash-for-food Through this intervention, the most vulnerable drought and flood-affected households will receive FSAC recommended cluster-recommended cash for food baskets for the period of four months
